Here’s a concise summary of what I know about the 1957 Soviet Cup in football (soccer), with notes where my memory is less certain:

- What it was: The 1957 edition of the USSR’s national knockout club competition (the Soviet Cup), played within the calendar-year season.
- Format: Single-elimination ties, typically one-leg matches; if drawn, replays were used rather than extra time/penalties (those came later). Early rounds were usually regionalized and included clubs from the top “Class A” division, “Class B,” and qualifiers from republican competitions.
- Winners: Lokomotiv Moscow. This was their second Soviet Cup title (their first was in 1936).
- Runners-up: My best recollection is Spartak Moscow.
- Final: Played in Moscow. I believe it was held at the Central Lenin Stadium (Luzhniki), which had opened in 1956, though some earlier finals had been at Dynamo Stadium. The score I recall is 1–0 for Lokomotiv.
- Notable player/decisive moment: I associate the winning goal with Valentin Bubukin for Lokomotiv, but I’m not 100% certain on the scorer.
- Coaching: Lokomotiv in that era was associated with Boris Arkadiev, one of Soviet football’s most prominent coaches; I believe he was at the helm around this time, but I can’t state with complete certainty that he managed the team specifically for the 1957 Cup run.
- Broader context: The Soviet Cup did not lead to European competition berths at that time; Soviet clubs didn’t enter UEFA competitions until the mid-1960s. The Cup was prestigious in its own right and often produced different winners than the league.
